doc: HF Inkling2Loop (Thinking Machines Inkling 2 Mini; text model only, model.llm.*) -> internal names = llama.cpp's inkling2 GGUF names (unsloth b12588-mix), so the native and GGUF routes share one vocabulary. Read by kit/test_hf_names_inkling2.py for coverage (each text key maps once, each GGUF name has an entry); not yet by inspect_safetensors.py, which has no MoE, loop or NVFP4 path. `prep` as in qwen35.json; `shape: true` = conv1d [C, 1, K] -> [K, C]; `transpose: true` = the converter transposes the matrix (internal shape = the HF shape, not its reverse); The vision tower (model.visual.*) and mtp.safetensors (DSpark) are out of scope here.

indexed._doc: model.llm.attn_res.* is indexed by layer outside the layer prefix: blk.{i}.attn_res_query = attn_queries.{i-1} (none on blk.0; [3, 2304] on the block-boundary layers 5, 11, 17, 23), blk.{i}.ffn_res_query = mlp_queries.{i}

nvfp4._doc: NVFP4 (modelopt layout): U8 = two e2m1 per byte (even element in the low nibble), F8_E4M3 scale per 16 values, per-expert F32 amax and one outer-scale denominator (2688 = 6 x 448); value = e2m1 x scale16 x amax / outer. GGUF (ggml NVFP4, 64-value blocks of 4 ue4m3 scales + 32 code bytes) keeps the per-16 scales and folds amax / outer into one F32 .scale per expert (`gguf_scale`). w13 rows interleave gate and up (even = gate); the GGUF converter de-interleaves them (gate rows first)

mxfp8._doc: MXFP8: F8_E4M3 values, U8 E8M0 scale per 32 (value = e4m3 x 2^(e8m0 - 127)); w13 rows interleave gate and up as in NVFP4. Unsloth's GGUFs carry these experts as BF16 (lossless upcast, de-interleaved), so the native route is the only one that keeps them 8-bit

value_checks: Checked 11-22 on values (byte-range reads of the native file against the Unsloth UD-Q8_K_XL GGUF): norms are copied as stored (bf16 -> f32, no +1; exact on embed_norm, norm, layer 0 attn/mlp norms); the GGUF's per-expert NVFP4 .scale = amax / outer_scale_denominator exactly (the denominator is 2688 = 6 x 448); native NVFP4 bytes hold the even element in the low nibble; native w13 rows interleave gate and up (even = gate, odd = up) and the GGUF de-interleaves them (gate rows 0-1151, up 1152-2303), for NVFP4 (layer 0) and MXFP8 (layer 20) alike, exact; the GGUF's BF16 copy of the MXFP8 experts is lossless.
